newsitem.title: USA: US announces $2 mln reward in al-Hayat bomb case.
newsitem.headline: US announces $2 mln reward in al-Hayat bomb case.

text.p: The United States on Thursday offered a $2 million reward for information leading to those responsible for four letter bombs sent to the Washington offices of the al-Hayat newspaper last January.

"It's clear to us that the people who were responsible for this letter bomb campaign intended to conduct a terrorism campaign in the United States and this is one of those important steps that we can in fact take to find the perpetrators," Greg Bujac, director of diplomatic security at the State Department, said at a briefing.
The reward will be publicized with posters and matchbooks and is part of a cooperative counter-terrorism arrangement between the State Department and the FBI, Bujac said.

Four letter bombs, disguised inside musical Christmas cards and bearing improvised explosive devices, were sent to offices of al-Hayat at the National Press Club, according to Tom Pickard, assistant director of the FBI's Washington field office.
All were postmarked Alexandria, Egypt, and dated Dec. 21, Pickard said.

Four similar bombs were discovered in London, four in New York City and three at Ft. Leavenworth, Kansas, Pickard said. No one was injured by the bombs found in the United States, but two people were hurt in London when one device went off.
All of the bombs were consistent, down to the addresses, size of the envelope and types of explosive devices used, Pickard said.
The London-based newspaper, owned by a member of the Saudi royal family, has a reputation as one of the most objective newspapers in the Arab world.
